headline: India's National Medical Commission has banned doctors and hospitals from using AI to invent patient testimonials, treatment results or endorsements in their advertising.
score_reason: Clear new rule with penalties and a direct AI link, but a national regulation in one country; kept at the curator score.
importance_line: Patients in India should meet fewer fabricated reviews and AI-made 'success stories' from clinics, but enforcement is untested.
source: The Economic Times and Deccan Chronicle
summary: The Economic Times and Deccan Chronicle report that the National Medical Commission, India's medical regulator, has issued advertising guidelines, in force immediately, that bar doctors and hospitals from using AI to fabricate patient experiences, treatment results, voices or endorsements, and also ban deepfakes, bought reviews and paid manipulation of search rankings. A first violation can bring a warning and ethics training, and a third can mean suspension of registration for three to six months.
notes: The Economic Times text is a short synopsis; details come from Deccan Chronicle (https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/nmc-bans-fake-ai-patient-reviews-misleading-medical-ads-1994209). Issue date of the guidelines ('earlier this week') is not exact.
